items.description: The plan never mentions the write-verb audit in tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py, which scans skills, commands and agents for `git commit`, `git push`, `git add`, `gh pr` and similar and requires each hit to be classified by its exact line text. Task 5's template and Tasks 1-4 and 7 add such lines, so the suite fails from Task 5 on and no task says how to fix it. Each task that adds or edits such a line must name that test file, add an exact-text classification entry in one of the five categories, and update the key when a classified line is edited.
items.plan_quote: do not run `/sc:implement`, `/task`, `git commit`, `git push` or `/sc:pr-submit`; print the plan path and `Waiting for approval`

items.description: The `worktree` subcommand output has no tracked-files field, yet Task 4's claim.md step must print 'untracked, do not stage' only when no file under the worktree's .dev/issues/<N>/ is tracked, and the script owns every git call. Also, when `git ls-files` fails, run() returns a failed result without raising, the tracked set reads as empty, and a differing tracked file would be renamed to .prev and overwritten. The output needs a machine-readable tracked-files field that tells 'none tracked' from 'unknown', and the copy must fail without overwriting when ls-files fails.
items.plan_quote: printing `{status, path, branch, match_key, warning, detail}` with `status` one of `created`, `reused`, `failed`.

items.description: The submit block of the launch template tells the agent to check for an open PR, which can be written as `gh pr list --head <branch>` with no `--repo`, and templates are outside the fork-safety scan (`_FORK_FILES`). A launched agent could reach the upstream repository while every test passes. Every gh call in the submit block must name `--repo IronbellyOrg/IronClaude`, and a test must scan the template.
items.plan_quote: check that no PR is already open or merged for the branch; commit with a conventional-commit message

items.description: Task 7 tells the implementer to replace the claim-mode return contract with the ten new fields, but SKILL.md:101-115 is one contract shared by both modes and carries `status`, `issue_number` and `next_steps_path`, which the claim still needs. A literal replacement drops them or changes create mode, and ST-10 (only checks the ten fields exist) would still pass. The correct change extends the shared contract and ST-10 also checks the kept fields.
items.plan_quote: replace the claim-mode return contract with the ten fields of design section 10

items.description: ST-4 bans the Orca link flags in the skill, refs, command and script but gives no matching rule. A substring scan fails on existing text (`--pr` is a prefix of `--prompt`; `--issue-url` already appears in claim.md and clickup_claim.py; the prose '--model flag' in tiers.md), and a line scan misses a wrapped argv list. The rule must match whole tokens on orca command lines only, exclude the launch call, and find the argv in orca_worktree.py by parsing it with ast.
items.plan_quote: ST-4 (no forbidden Orca flag in skill, refs, command or script outside the launch call)

items.description: Several required tests and safeguards have no owning task: LA-7 is not among LA-1 to LA-6, ARG-1 (bad or missing arguments exit 2) is tested only on `preflight`, ST-5's template row and ST-6's Wave 8 half are unpinned, and Task 6 drops the detail telling the user to check Orca before re-running after a timeout, the note that a hand-started agent is not governed by the hook, and the rule that the pending record stays. An implementer builds none of them. Task 6 must add LA-7 and assertions for the dropped safeguards, and Tasks 2, 5 and 6 one ARG-1 case each.

The acceptance runs of Tasks 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 use -k filters and never run the whole file, so the gap only closes late. The rows should be added in the tasks that create the files.

items.description: The launch and worktree outputs have a single `warning` field holding only the code that set the status, but two codes can apply at once (W-ENFORCEMENT-ABSENT with W-LAUNCH-NOT-CCSESSION; W-ORIGIN-BASE-STALE with the .prev W-WORKTREE-COPY-FAILED). The remedy for the dropped code is lost, and `enforcement_hook` has no value on `already_launched`. The design must state precedence or carry every code, and define the hook value.
items.plan_quote: The warning field holds the one code that set the status; any other problem goes in `detail`.

The plan must not replace the prompt file when a launch record already exists.

items.description: Task 1's run() helper returns a failed result for a timeout, a nonzero exit or a missing binary without marking the timeout apart. Task 2 must treat a create that times out differently (list again) from a nonzero create exit (fail at once). An implementer builds a run() that cannot tell them apart, so a worktree created during a timeout is reported failed with no record. run() must mark timeouts and Task 2 needs an FO case for it.
items.plan_quote: returns a failed result (never raises) on timeout, nonzero exit or missing binary.
